note: Fernet (github.com/fernet/spec) in FL over aes:encrypt, hmac:digest and base64: version 0x80, an 8-byte time, a 16-byte IV, AES-128-CBC with PKCS#7, HMAC-SHA256, url-safe base64 with padding. The input is bytes and the token is its text as bytes. The key is a key param: 32 bytes, or their url-safe base64 text (the form CyberChef takes; 43 or 44 characters), anything else E_RANGE. The IV comes from the host CSPRNG (the +random effect) and the time from the clock (+time), as in CyberChef, so the output differs on every call; nothing falls back to Math.random (a host with no crypto.getRandomValues is E_PRIMITIVE). Tests pin both through the private fernet:_seal.

The inverse, with the HMAC checked before anything is decrypted (E_COERCE for a bad token, a wrong key, bad base64, a bad version byte or bad padding). The key is the same key param as in fernet:encrypt. CyberChef fixes the TTL at 0 (no time check); an added ttl param (seconds, default 0 = no check) applies the spec's age rules: older than the TTL, or more than 60 seconds in the future, is E_COERCE. The base64 padding is optional on input.

RFC 7519 over RFC 7515, in FL over hmac:digest. Only the HMAC algorithms HS256, HS384 and HS512 are offered; CyberChef's RS, ES and PS algorithms are public-key and belong to wave 7, and None (an unsigned token) is deliberately not offered. The key is a key param (not empty, else E_RANGE). The input is the payload JSON text and is signed exactly as given (it is not parsed or re-serialised, because FL has no JSON parser; it must be a JSON object by its first and last character, else E_COERCE). The header is {"alg":...,"typ":"JWT"} followed by the members of the header param (a JSON object text; typ there replaces the default, alg there is E_RANGE), where CyberChef merges a parsed object.

Verifies HS256, HS384 and HS512 under the key and returns the payload as the JSON text the token holds, as CyberChef returns the payload (a failure raises E_COERCE, there is no bool). The alg param is auto (the token's own header chooses among the three HMAC algorithms, which is safe because only a shared secret is accepted) or a pinned algorithm. alg none is never accepted, whatever the key or pin (E_RANGE), and neither is any algorithm that is not HS256/384/512 (RS, ES and PS are wave 7: E_RANGE). A header with the text "alg" twice is ambiguous (E_COERCE). Unlike CyberChef (jsonwebtoken) the exp and nbf claims are not checked: this is a signature check, because that needs a JSON parser and a clock.

Splits a compact token and decodes the payload (or, with the part param, the header), without a key, as the JSON text the token holds, exactly as written (CyberChef returns the parsed payload). Each decoded part must be a JSON object by its first and last character, and the token three parts (an encrypted five-part JWT is E_COERCE); the JSON is not parsed further because FL has no JSON parser.

itsdangerous's URLSafeTimedSerializer as Flask uses it, in FL over base64. Decodes the payload.timestamp.signature cookie to the session JSON text as written (not parsed). The View TimeStamp option is the timestamp param (default false); with it the result is {"payload":...,"timestamp":N}. The timestamp is read as itsdangerous writes it, the shortest big-endian integer, where CyberChef reads exactly 4 bytes. A cookie whose payload Flask compressed with zlib (it starts with a dot) is E_COERCE with a message saying decompression comes with the compression vocabulary, because the runtime has no inflate yet (CyberChef cannot read these either).

Signs a session JSON as a Flask cookie: salt cookie-session by default, the 'hmac' key derivation HMAC(secret, salt), a SHA-1 (default) or SHA-256 signature over payload.timestamp, url-safe base64 without padding. The key and the salt are key params (CyberChef's toggle encodings, minus Decimal and Binary which are chain steps); an empty key is E_RANGE (Secret key required) and an empty salt means the default, as CyberChef. The input JSON text is used as given. The time is the clock (the +time effect) unless the added timestamp param pins it (Unix seconds above 0; 0 is now), which also makes the word reproducible. Never compresses.

Checks the signature as flask-session:sign writes it (E_COERCE when it does not verify, as CyberChef's Invalid signature) and returns {"valid":true,"payload":...} with ,"timestamp":N when the timestamp param is set (default true), as text rather than a parsed object. Same key, salt and algorithm params as flask-session:sign. A compressed (leading dot) payload is E_COERCE until the compression vocabulary exists. The age of the cookie is not checked, as in CyberChef.
